hints: Use $P = Fv$, noting that at constant speed the forward driving force equals the resistance force of $650\text{ N}$.
Compute $650 \times 30 = 19500\text{ W}$ and convert to kW.
walkthrough:
At constant speed, acceleration is zero, so the engine's driving force $F$ equals the resistance force $R$:
$$F = R = 650\text{ N}$$

State the formula for mechanical power:
$$P = Fv$$

Substitute $F = 650\text{ N}$ and $v = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$P = 650 \times 30 = 19500\text{ W}$$

Convert watts to kilowatts by dividing by 1000:
$$P = \frac{19500}{1000} = 19.5\text{ kW}$$

hints: Calculate the new driving force using the increased power $P = 19.5 + 9 = 28.5\text{ kW} = 28500\text{ W}$ at $v = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Apply Newton's second law: $950 - 650 = 1300a$, and solve for $a = \frac{3}{13}\text{ m s}^{-2} \approx 0.231\text{ m s}^{-2}$.
walkthrough:
Calculate the new power developed by the engine when increased by $9\text{ kW} = 9000\text{ W}$:
$$P_{\text{new}} = 19500 + 9000 = 28500\text{ W}$$

Find the new driving force $F_{\text{new}}$ at the instant the car is travelling at $v = 30\text{ m s}^{-1}$:
$$F_{\text{new}} = \frac{P_{\text{new}}}{v} = \frac{28500}{30} = 950\text{ N}$$

Apply Newton's second law $F_{\text{net}} = ma$ along the horizontal direction of motion:
$$F_{\text{new}} - R = ma$$
$$950 - 650 = 1300a$$
$$300 = 1300a$$

Divide both sides by 1300 to solve for acceleration $a$:
$$a = \frac{300}{1300} = \frac{3}{13}\text{ m s}^{-2}\quad (\approx 0.23077\text{ m s}^{-2})$$
$$a = 0.231\text{ m s}^{-2}\quad (\text{to 3 significant figures})$$

hints: Identify all forces acting parallel to the downward slope: forward driving force $\frac{11500}{v}$, downward weight component $mg\sin\theta$, and opposing resistance $1000 + 20v$.
Form the equilibrium equation down the slope: $\frac{11500}{v} + 1300(10)(0.08) - (1000 + 20v) = 0$.
Simplify to $\frac{11500}{v} + 40 - 20v = 0$, and multiply by $v$ to obtain the quadratic $v^2 - 2v - 575 = 0$.
Solve the quadratic equation to find the positive speed $v = 25\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough: List all forces acting parallel to the road as the car travels downwards:
Driving force of the engine down the incline: $F = \frac{P}{v} = \frac{11500}{v}$
Component of weight acting down the incline: $W_{\parallel} = mg\sin\theta = (1300)(10)(0.08) = 1040\text{ N}$
Resistance to motion acting up the incline: $R = 1000 + 20v$

Because the speed is constant, acceleration is zero ($a = 0\text{ m s}^{-2}$). Set the net force down the plane to zero:
$$\frac{11500}{v} + 1040 - (1000 + 20v) = 0$$
$$\frac{11500}{v} + 40 - 20v = 0$$
